chunks.text: OUR ROOTS OUR STORY OUR LEGACY OUR FUTURE An elegant family home for the photographs, stories, genealogy, and enduring heritage of the Glymph family. explore our story ABOUT GLYMPHVILLE Where legacy becomes living memory Glymphville is more than a website. It is a family home on the web –a place where names become stories, photographs become inheritance,and each generation can see itself as part of something lasting.At its heart are Frank and Deliah Glymph, whose strength, grace,and presence continue to shape the family’s identity. This space isdesigned to honor that foundation while creating room for reunionmemories, family history, photographs, and the branches stillgrowing forward. We laugh together; we cry together. We are GLYMPH’S! Frank Glymph was 100% Nigerian. He was born into and freed from slavery in Newberry, South Carolina, where he met and married Lide. Five children were born from this union. They were Henrietta, Laura Ann, Drucilla, Edward George and Carrie Glymph. chunks.title: A Legacy That Lives On
chunks.text: As the family grew, so did its story. New generations brought fresh energy, new ideas, and new dreams, yet the essence of the family remained unchanged. The values passed down — integrity, kindness, perseverance — became a guiding force in every chapter. Stories from the past turned into lessons for the future. The experiences of one generation inspired the next, creating a continuous flow of wisdom and growth. Each member became both a guardian of the past and a contributor to the future. Today, the legacy is not just remembered — it is lived every day. It exists in the way people support each other, in the respect they carry, and in the dreams they continue to pursue.

chunks.title: Strength in Unity
chunks.text: Throughout the years, one thing remained constant — the strength of togetherness. No matter what life brought, the family faced it side by side. Challenges were never seen as individual burdens, but as shared responsibilities. There were moments of uncertainty, times when the future seemed unclear, but unity always brought clarity. Conversations around the table, support during difficult decisions, and celebrations of even the smallest achievements created a deep sense of belonging. This bond didn’t just make life easier — it made it meaningful. It taught every member that no matter how far they go, they are always connected by something stronger than distance or time.

chunks.title: Where It All Began (1980)
chunks.text: In 1980, the journey began with a vision that was simple yet powerful — to build a life rooted in stability, respect, and family values. There were no guarantees of success, only a strong belief that hard work and unity would pave the way forward. The early years were filled with challenges. Resources were limited, and every decision carried weight. Yet, what stood out was the determination to never give up. Small milestones — a new opportunity, a growing household, shared meals — became symbols of progress. Over time, what started as a single step grew into a steady path. The foundation built during those years continues to support every generation that followed. It is a reminder that great stories often begin quietly, with courage and consistency.

This is not about us being boastful...it's a mere fact. ` If Frank and Lide were alive today, they would certainly be bragging about their family. Look at what we have given to this world. From the days they lived in Newberry, SC, born into slavery, they surely couldn't have imagined their descendants branching out this far wide. The unity, strength, honor and will of this family speaks for itself. But, as we all know, none of us will mind telling you. WE ARE GLYMPHS! This year the Glymph family celebrates its 20th family reunion. Spanning over forty-three years, and ten (10) states, this rich tradition has grown into much more than a family cookout. In the late 1970s, Asberry "Al" Glymph, out of the love for his family and commitment

chunks.title: 2023-Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2023-Columbia-SC
chunks.text: to ensure that his children, nieces and nephews grew to know and love one another planned family trips that would take his brothers and sisters and their families to Virginia Beach and Myrtle Beach, SC. These trips would spark the idea that laid the foundation for what would become the first Glymph Family Reunion. Unfortunately, Al passed away before seeing the fruits of his labor when the inaugural Glymph Family Reunion was held back at the home place in Newberry, SC in 1980. There was participation by both the young and old, near and far. Stories were shared and the experiences that brought us all together were evidenced that weekend. The family voted to continue the tradition and agreed to rotate the host location to cities in which large numbers of family resided. Family members from the host site formed committees to orchestrate the much anticipated reunions and ensure that the reunions continued. Our gatherings took us to Cleveland, OH (1981), Rochelle Park, NJ (1983), Newberry, SC (1987), Detroit, MI (1989), Cleveland, OH (1991), and Newberry, SC (1994). In 1996

chunks.title: 2023-Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2023-Columbia-SC
chunks.text: the torch was passed down to the next generation who took the lead in planning its first reunion in Virginia Beach, VA. Reunions continued in Detroit, MI (2000), Atlanta, GA (2002), Cleveland, OH (2004). Wanting to keep the reunions fresh and to incorporate the ideas of more family members, the family embraced the era of technology to coordinate destination reunions, by reconstructing the committee format to include representatives from various states. The reunions continued to flourish; participation grew and yielded additional outreach for Glymphs to become involved. Destination reunions have taken us to Myrtle Beach, SC, (2006), and Pigeon Forge, TN (2008); we returned to the home place of Newberry, SC (2010), Ocean City, MD, (2012), Wilmington, NC (2014) and Cleveland, OH (2016), and Savannah, GA (2018). The 2020 gathering that was scheduled to take place in Columbia, SC underwent a remarkable transformation, due to the COVID pandemic. We yearned for the cherished physical togetherness, yet fate dictated a virtual reunion for the Glymph family. This unprecedented circumstance created an opportunity to utilize the power of technology, linking our dispersed

chunks.title: 2023-Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2023-Columbia-SC
chunks.text: clans, as well as welcoming new families into our embrace, scattered across the nation. As we emerge from the COVID crisis, we confront an ever-changing world, evolving before our eyes. For our 20th reunion, we are resolute in our determination to honor our family aspirations, bringing us back to the home state, South Carolina. While each reunion has certainly been different, all have offered the perfect platform to learn more about the rich Glymph history, reconnect with family, enjoy the offerings of the host city, and most importantly, always remember... chunks.text: GLYMPH’S! Frank Glymph was 100% Nigerian. He was born into and freed from slavery in Newberry, South Carolina, where he met and married Lide. Five children were born from this union. They were Henrietta, Laura Ann, Drucilla, Edward George and Carrie Glymph. In addition, Frank and Lide raised their grandson Frank “Tack” Chaplin Glymph Edward George was the only son of Frank and Lide. When E. George came of age, he married Minnie Lyles Richardson, and they were blessed with three sons: Ulysses, Clarence, and George. Minnie died shortly after the birth of her last son and E. George later married Sarah Ann Richardson, Minnie’s sister. E George was a farmer and in 1908 he purchased 59 acres of land in Newberry County where he raised his sons and grandchildren. Ulysses Glymph, who was the oldest, worked as a farmer for many years in Newberry County. In later years he operated a sawmill. He soon took up with his wife Mattie Ruff and they had 10 children Minnie, James, Asberry, George, Ulysses, Lily Mae, Heyward, Johnny, Woodrow and Pounee. Clarence

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: Glymph, the second oldest son, married Dolly Ruff and they were blessed with seven children Bertha Lee, Claudia, Blanche, Beatrice, Clarence, Jr, Thomas and Dolly. He left Newberry County in 1920 where he settled in Gaffney, South Carolina to become a prominent businessman and civic leader. George Glymph, although the youngest son was the first to move to Gaffney and he invites his brother Clarence to join him after receiving his dentistry degree at Meharry Medical College. George became a dentist and later established his practice in Spartanburg South Carolina. He married Vivian Cottingham, and they had four children, Mildred, Harold, Helen, and George Jr. The fruit that Frank and Lide produced is alive and well. today the Glymph Family is spread throughout the United States. You can find someone from the Glymph Family Tree mastering any profession imaginable. We have become doctors, lawyers, government workers, politicians, teachers, engineers, first responders, factory workers, authors, media professions, business professionals, and business owners. We also have many college students, retirees and babies which keep our fruit alive. You name it and we’re

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: doing it. This is not about us being boastful. It’s just mere facts. If Frank and Lide were alive today, they would certainly be bragging about their family. Look at what we have given to this world. From the days they lived in Newberry, SC, born into slavery, they surely couldn’t have imagined their descendants branching out this far and wide. The unity, strength, honor and will of this family speaks for itself. But, as we all know, none of us will mind telling you... “WE ARE GLYMPHS!!!” 14 History GLYMPH FAMILY GLYMPH FAMILY This year, the Glymph family celebrates its 21st family reunion. Spanning over forty- five years and ten states this rich tradition has grown into much more than a family cookout. In the late 1970s Asberry “A.B.” Glymph, out of the love for his family and commitment to ensure that his children, nieces and nephews grew to know and love one another, planned family trips that would take his brothers and sisters and their families to Virginia Beach, Virginia and Myrtle Beach, South Carolina. These trips would

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: spark the idea that laid the foundation for what would become the first Glymph family reunion. Unfortunately, A.B. passed away before seeing the fruits of his labor when the inaugural Glymph family reunion was held back at the “Home” place in Newberry, South Carolina in 1980. There was participation by both the young and old, near and far. Stories were shared, and the experiences that brought us all together were evidenced that weekend. The family voted to continue the tradition and agreed to rotate the host location to cities in which large numbers of families resided. Family members from the host site formed committees to orchestrate the much-anticipated reunion and ensure that the reunions continued. Our gatherings took us to Cleveland, Ohio in 1981, Rochelle Park, New Jersey in 1983, Newberry, South Carolina in 1987, Detroit, Michigan in 1989, Cleveland, Ohio in 1991, and back to Newberry South Carolina in 1994, at which the torch was passed down to the next generation who took the lead and planned their first reunion in 1996 in Virginia Beach, Virginia. Reunions continued in

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: Detroit, Michigan in 2000, Atlanta, Georgia in 2002 and Cleveland, Ohio in 2004. Wanting to keep the reunions fresh and to incorporate the ideas of more family members, the family embraced the use of technology to coordinate destination reunions by reconstructing the committee format to include representatives from various states. The reunions continued to flourish, participation grew and yielded additional outreach for Glymph’s to become involved. Destination reunions have taken us to Myrtle Beach, South Carolina in 2006 and Pigeon Forge, Tennessee in 2008, we returned to the home place of Newberry, South Carolina in 2010, Ocean City, Maryland in 2012, Wilmington, North Carolina in 2014, Cleveland, Ohio in 2016, and Savannah, Georgia in 2018. The 2020 reunion that was scheduled to take place in Columbia, South Carolina underwent a remarkable transformation due to the COVID-19 pandemic. We yearned for the cherished physical togetherness, yet fate dictated a virtual reunion for the Glymph family. This unprecedented circumstance created an opportunity to utilize the power of technology, linking our dispersed clans, as well as welcoming new families into our embrace, scattered

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: across the nation. As we emerged from the global crisis, we confronted an ever-changing world evolving before our eyes for our 20th reunion. We were resolute in our determination to honor our family aspirations that brought us back to the home state, South Carolina, in 2023, a tradition we have incorporated to occur every 10 years. This reunion is taking us back to a state that we have previously hosted. We made such joyous memories in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee that this time we visit Nashville for new ones.. While each reunion has certainly been different, all have offered the perfect platform to learn more about the rich Glymph history, reconnect with family, enjoy the offerings of the host city and most importantly always remember...We are GLYMPH’S....we are nine-generations strong. We all we got! 15 Reunion History 16 WELCOMING ANDREW’S BRANCH WELCOMING ANDREW’S BRANCH Frank's Brother Andrew’s branch A Brotherhood Reunited Through DNA In 2023, for the first time, we learned through DNA testing something remarkable: Frank had a older brother—Andrew. Born in 1827, Andrew’s existence had never been part of

chunks.text: the known family story. No one alive today could say how he ended up in Arkansas, while Frank remained in South Carolina. But the discovery shed light on a bond that had long been lost to history, buried by time and the cruel displacements caused by slavery. We can only imagine what happened after the two brothers were freed. Perhaps Andrew, still young, chose to leave, searching for an opportunity or simply a new beginning. Somehow, he found his way to Arkansas, where his branch of the family tree took root—separated from Frank’s, but never severed. Back in 1986, decades before DNA could connect people across generations, Linda, her mother, grandmother, and four others made a journey to South Carolina. They came looking for family. They had always heard that their people were from South Carolina, but they didn’t have names or concrete connections—only stories and instincts passed down through generations. While there, they met James A. Glymph, George Glymph, and Walter Glymph. The men welcomed them with warmth and curiosity. Though they couldn’t pinpoint the exact relationship at the

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: time, they believed there had to be a connection. They showed Linda’s family around, shared what they knew, and kept the door open. That trip planted a seed. Over the years, the rise of DNA technology revolutionized how families—especially Black families separated during slavery—could reconnect. What oral history couldn’t confirm, DNA could begin to trace. And little by little, Frank’s bloodline began appearing within Andrew’s. Distant cousins, shared genetic markers, overlapping trees. What once was speculation became fact: Frank and Andrew were brothers. This discovery was more than just a scientific match—it was a restoration of lost family. It brought clarity to the stories Linda’s family had always held onto. It confirmed the hunches of the Glymph’s back in 1986. It gave two fractured branches of a family a shared beginning. Their reunion may be separated by decades, but their story is now whole again. 17 Frank's older Brother, Andrew PASSING THE TORCH PASSING THE TORCH 18 From Generation 6 to 7 PAST REUNION PAST REUNION 19 1981 Cleveland, OH Johnnie Glymph Juanita Glymph Lizzie “Dank” Glymph Robert “Soc” Glymph

She was the cherished daughter of the late Johnnie and Lizzie Glymph and the younger sister of Robert Glymph (Juanita). Seeking a better life for their family, her father relocated them to Cleveland, Ohio, where Johnnie thrived. A bright and active student, she was a proud member of her school's safety patrol, served as a majorette in the band, and was a secretary for the school’s booster club. She graduated from John Hay High School and went on to further her education at The Ohio State University and Cleveland State University. In 1965, Johnnie married the love of her life, James Thomas. Their union was blessed with two sons, Sean and Brent Thomas, to whom she devoted her life. Her passion for nurturing children extended beyond her own home — Johnnie began her career in education as a preschool teacher and was part of one of the first Head Start programs in Cleveland. In 1968, the Thomas

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: family moved to Detroit, Michigan, and eventually settled in Southfield, where Johnnie continues to reside. After spending five years as a stay-at-home mother, she joined Southfield Public Schools as a paraprofessional. Over a dedicated 31-year career, she made a lasting impact on students and staff alike. She was a union representative, an advocate for children, and the recipient of multiple awards recognizing her devotion and service. 21 GLYMPH FAMILY GLYMPH FAMILY Matriarch JOHNNIE MAE GLYMPH THOMAS 22 Education remained a cornerstone of her life, both professionally and personally. As her sons attended school in Southfield, Johnnie was an ever-present and active parent — participating in the PTA and serving on numerous parent-led committees. Her unwavering support and involvement were pivotal in her sons' academic journeys. Tragedy struck in 1986 when Johnnie lost her husband James to cancer. With courage and the support of her family, she took on the role of both parents, never wavering in her commitment to her sons. Faith and community were guiding forces in Johnnie’s life. Influenced by her mother’s example, she became deeply involved in

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1

Her roots run deep in the Dorset Street neighborhood, where she is a respected and beloved member of a close-knit community. Even after retiring from Southfield Public Schools, Johnnie continued to give back — working at Macy’s and caring for her elderly neighbor until she passed away at the remarkable age of 108. She remains active, enjoying regular outings with her "Birthday Crew," a group of lifelong friends and former colleagues. Proud of her Black heritage, Johnnie has passed down this pride and strength to her sons and her heart and soul — her granddaughter, Brielle. Her legacy is one of service, strength, and love — a life beautifully lived and still inspiring others. GLYMPH FAMILY GLYMPH FAMILY Matriarch JOHNNIE MAE GLYMPH THOMAS cont... Many have asked where Robert got his nickname “Socrates.” It was Dr. and Mrs. Moore who gave him the nickname, and the family kept it going by affectionately calling him “Soc.” People he grew up with still call him by that name today. Robert’s parents’ stay in the Biltmore Estates community was short-lived when his father chose to relocate to the North to find work in Ohio. Robert grew up in the Cleveland Metropolitan Housing Projects, but as a child, he loved spending summers down South visiting family. He attended Shiloh Baptist Church and was baptized on May 22, 1955. During high school, he worked at Huron Road Hospital and later joined his Uncle Woodrow Glymph at the Excel Cellophane Company. That job eventually afforded him his first car—a yellow and white Ford Fairlane. Many of his friends labeled him “Cool Bob” after that purchase. Robert graduated from East Technical High School on June 15, 1959, and married his wife, Juanita, a few years later on August 12, 1962. He

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: joined the U.S. Army that same year, where he played basketball on the Army team and worked in Signal Corps Communications. While serving, he was awarded a Good Conduct Medal and a Marksman Badge (Rifle-MI). Robert and Juanita became the proud parents of a son and daughter: Robert John Glymph, born on September 9, 1963, who recently passed away on May 18, 2025, after battling numerous health complications, and Jennifer Lisa Glymph, born on December 2, 1966. In addition to his sister, Johnnie Glymph-Thomas, Robert is the uncle of Sean and Brent Thomas. He also has a son- in-law, Byron “Big B” Horne. After 42 years of dedicated service, Robert retired from General Motors Corporation. After enjoying a bit of well- earned rest, he took on a new role as a School Crossing Guard for the City of Beachwood. He served in that role for 14 years until retiring recently due to health challenges. Robert enjoys all types of music—though he often jokes that he doesn’t understand a thing about rap. His favorite pastimes include reading the newspaper and watching

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1

He finds great joy in spending time with his wife Juanita, his grandchildren—Robin, Jillian, Britany, Jasmine—and his step-granddaughter, Bianca. He also cherishes his great-grandchildren: Brooklyn, Jackson, Braxton, Bradley, Jacob, Kamila, and Khalid. The older girls do their best to keep him on his toes—often correcting his grammar and playfully teasing him about his hilarious mispronunciations. These moments are filled with laughter, love, and learning—hallmarks of their time together. Robert is always making sure that his family has everything they need and want—by whatever means necessary. He takes great pride in his children’s and grandchildren’s accomplishments and continuously encourages them to strive for their best. He stands firmly on the values of respect, honesty, independence, and—above all—love for one another. These are not just words to Robert; they are principles he lives by and instills in every member of his family. Outside the family, Robert—affectionately known by many as “Uncle Soc”—finds deep purpose in helping others. Always ready to lend a hand, he is

chunks.text: James "Billy" Glymph, Sr. also affectionately known as Boo, Daddy, Dad, Bossman, GrandDaddy, Heavy, Jimmy, Uncle Billy, Godfather, etc. was born February 4, 1942, to the union of Asberry B. Glymph, Sr. and Electia Henderson Glymph, in Newberry County, South Carolina. Billy was the fifth child of ten siblings: Thelma, Bessie, Ulysses, Asberry, Clarence, George, Walter, Tommy and Essie. As a young man, he played baseball and was a member of Fellowship Baptist Church in Newberry, South Carolina. He attended Gallman High School in Newberry County and in 1961 at nineteen (19), he left South Carolina and moved to Brooklyn, New York to find work. After being in New York for a couple of years with his brothers, Billy went back to South Carolina to bring the love of his life and grade school sweetheart, Leola “Lee” Sims, to New York. They were married on July 23, 1966. While they were married for almost 58 years, their love affair began 66 years ago in 1958. While in New York he worked at Ford Motor Company in Mahwah, New Jersey, until

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: his retirement in 1980. He then became an independent owner with Great Neck Taxi, Inc., of Great Neck, New York, until his retirement in 1991. He then returned to his homestead and utilized his entrepreneurial drive and transportation experience to become the co- owner of Glymph Brothers Taxi in Newberry, South Carolina. Glymph Brothers Taxi was one of the first black-owned businesses in Newberry County. Even though he returned back to homestead of Newberry, South Carolina, he never lost his love and passion for sports and celebrating the New York Yankees, New York Giants and New York Knicks. He supported his favorite teams by traveling to see them play. Or staying local and hosting Playoffs and Super Bowl parties for family and close friends. Billy was a hard working, family loving man and a father figure to many. Family meant a great deal to Billy and while raising his own family, Billy took on the extra responsibility of helping to raise many of his nieces and nephews. He was always present to celebrate family milestones such as birthdays, graduations, holiday

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: dinners, weddings and one of his favorites... Glymph Family Reunions! Billy never missed one Glymph Family Reunion. He attended all twenty-five Glymph Family Reunions, wherever and whenever they occurred. He enjoyed spending time with family, new and old generations, reminiscing about old times and strategizing for the future. He also had a jokester side to him, he would pick or joke around with family members, giving them a hard time which was his way of showing affection towards you. If he didn’t give you a hard time, he felt like he didn’t care about you. He always wanted everyone to succeed in whatever their passion or expertise was. And he would offer any support that he could to make that dream become a reality. In his spare time he enjoyed playing cards, traveling and spending time with family and friends, while being a connoisseur of many food delicacies. Left to carry out his legacy is Billy’s Branch: Leola “Lee”, Lisa, Todd Sr., James “J.J” Jr. Anita, Taylor, Asia, Todd “TJ” Jr., and Javarius “Lil Jay”. 25 GLYMPH FAMILY GLYMPH FAMILY

chunks.text: Spotlight JAMES “BILLY” GLYMPH, SR Born May 11, 1970 in Brooklyn, New York, raised in Rosedale, Queens, Alvin Glymph is the third child of Asberry A.B. Glymph, Jr. and Shirley Gloria Glymph. A true cornerstone of the Glymph family, Alvin’s commitment to kin runs deep—frequently traveling across the country from his home in Atlanta to show up, support, and celebrate with loved ones. Rarely missing a milestone, he lives out the values of family through consistent and heartfelt action. Alvin’s character blends logical, thoughtful leadership with an infectious, fun-loving spirit that uplifts those around him. Whether mentoring younger relatives, or launching joint business ventures with family, Alvin leads by example, embodying the Glymph family’s entrepreneurial and collaborative ethos. th Inspired by his mother, who ran two successful businesses—a home childcare service and a school transportation company. Alvin founded Glymph and Associates in 2000. His firm specializes in technical assistance and business development for nonprofits, small businesses, and public-sector organizations. From creating logic models to developing evaluation plans and data-driven strategies, G & A has helped improve outcomes for children and

chunks.title: Glymph-Family-Reunion-Book-2025-1
chunks.text: families across the nation. A nationally recognized leader in child well-being, sustainability, and strategic partnerships, Alvin brings over three decades of experience in program evaluation, needs assessments, and organizational development. In 2022, he joined United Way of Greater Atlanta as Vice President of Strategic Partnerships. In 2025, he was promoted to Chief Community Impact Officer, where he now leads grant-making strategies that address systemic barriers to opportunity and economic mobility for children and families in the region. Previously, Alvin held senior roles at DeKalb County School District and Project GRAD Atlanta and contributed to university-based research at Georgia State University. His expertise has made him a trusted advisor to foundations, school districts, government agencies, and community organizations. Alvin earned his B.A. in Religion from Colgate University in 1991—where he met his future wife, Gina Burris. The couple married in 1995 and will celebrate their 30th wedding anniversary August 6th of this year. They have two adult children: Alvin “A.B.” Glymph, a teacher, and Adayah Glymph a registered nurse. Alvin later earned his M.A. in Educational Research from Emory University in

FAMILY FAMILY With hearts full of love and sorrow, we celebrate the life of J.R. @ Tommy Henry Glymph, Jr., 47, of Pfafftown, NC, who peacefully transitioned into eternal life on July 31, 2025. He was born on May 23, 1978 in Newberry, SC, to the late Tommy H. Glymph, Sr. and Loraine Ingram :Elgin, SC;. He was the baby and their only son. J.R. was a logical@ mathematical intellect, a man of creative brilliance and dedication, with an unwavering devotion to his family. He shared life with his wife, Ladine Glymph, and their two sons, Ladanian Vasquez and Lincoln Glymph, calling Atlanta, GA home until their journey brought them to Winston@Salem, NC in 2016. From a young age, it was clear that J.R. was a genius. His mind moved with quiet power, consistently pondering, consistently observing. To know J.R. was to be delightfully challenged with thoughtful perspectives, deep conversations, and genuine interest

chunks.title: Glymph_-Tommy-JR
chunks.text: in lifeMs details. Whether it was trivia about world capitals, obscure movie quotes, or historic Jfirsts,K his love for knowledge went beyond the factsCit was about helping people think, laugh, and connect. He saw the world as a giant playground of curiosity, bursting with wonder and stories just waiting to be discovered. Baptized at Fellowship Baptist Church in Pomaria, SC, and educated in Newberry County public schools, J.R. grew into a stellar athlete and proud member of the Newberry High School class of 1996. He furthered his education and lent his athletic football talents to the University of South Carolina, Hampton University, and Benedict College. His professional journey included BCBS of SC, Pepsi, Herbalife, and up until his passing, TriMark in Winston@Salem, NC. J.R. volunteered as a coach for his sonMs team, the South Fork Panthers. He enjoyed being in support of his community through charity and time. 1995 NHS Blocking Award 1987 Jets Little League Champs 1992 NHS Offensive Lineman of the Year 1990 Willingham MVP 1994 NHS Peach Blossom AAA All-Region 1988 Jets Best Defensive Player 1995 NHS

He was a relentless seeker of growth, constantly embracing challenges and rediscovering talents from his past, like drawing and rekindling bonds with influential figures in his life. His voice and words carried power, purpose, and poetry. Whether shaping thoughts into prose, rap, or verse, he offered clarity and depth that reflected an extraordinary mind. Through his musical talent, he brought light and joy to those around him, crafting lyrics infused with artistry, genuine heart, and soul.
